evals.prompt: The /api/copilotkit stream is returning 500 after a runtime change. Diagnose the CopilotKit side without rewriting Mastra tools.
evals.expected_output: Routes to CopilotKit plus systematic debugging; verifies installed v2/runtime wiring and current official sources before proposing a change.
expectations: Uses CopilotKit for the browser/runtime boundary
Verifies installed/current source rather than answering volatile API details from memory
Does not rewrite Mastra tool business logic

evals.prompt: A Mastra search tool executes successfully but the CopilotKit v2 card never renders. What should we verify?
evals.expected_output: Checks frontend action/tool registration against the Mastra tool-map key, AG-UI result flow, and rendered browser path.
expectations: Checks the CopilotKit action/tool-name contract
Checks AG-UI/tool result handling
Requires browser-visible proof, not only a tool unit test

evals.prompt: The event host publishing rule needs to change from draft-only to draft-or-reviewed.
evals.expected_output: Does not select CopilotKit as the owner because this is a product-domain rule with no CopilotKit dependency.
expectations: Does not treat CopilotKit as the primary owner
Routes to the relevant product/domain workflow instead

evals.prompt: Can we copy a CopilotKit main-branch example into our app? We are on the pinned @copilotkit/react-core.
evals.expected_output: Checks installed package/version and pinned/current official source first; preserves v2 import/runtime contract and refuses blind latest-main copying.
expectations: Checks installed version before using examples
Does not blindly substitute latest-main API behavior
Preserves the v2 surface when applicable

evals.prompt: CopilotKit verify says MDE has no hosted project/API key. Diagnose our self-hosted /api/copilotkit runtime safely without signing into Intelligence or making an unrequested live model call.
evals.expected_output: Runs OSS wiring-only verify with --expect-runtime oss and --agent id; adds --runtime-url/auth headers if needed. Makes --round-trip an explicitly authorized QA step because it consumes model credits and creates a thread; no default production round-trip.
expectations: Uses --expect-runtime oss with an explicit agent id for a wiring-only check
Uses --round-trip only as an opt-in live QA test and explains cost/thread persistence
Does not connect hosted Intelligence or claim wiring checks prove full user journeys

evals.prompt: We may add an MDE Slack agent later. Where should CopilotKit guidance come from, and should we put the Channel host inside our Vercel Next.js route now?
evals.expected_output: Routes through the canonical MDE CopilotKit skill to the vendored Channels references, explains that vendoring guidance does not enable Channels, and rejects a serverless request route as the long-running Channel host.
expectations: Keeps copilotkit as the single MDE skill owner
Uses the vendored Channels references
Does not enable or host managed Channels inside the existing serverless request route

evals.prompt: During prelaunch development a renter requests a viewing for a test apartment that has no landlord verification or partner approval. Should we add a useHumanInTheLoop approval requirement before allowing the viewing?
evals.expected_output: No Phase A business-approval gate. HITL can support user confirmation on consequential actions, but it must not require property eligibility, landlord approval, verification, or paperwork; retain authenticated backend authority and durable writes.
expectations: Rejects landlord/partner/eligibility paperwork as a Phase A prerequisite
Distinguishes user confirmation from business approval and from server authorization
Preserves auth, isolation and atomic/idempotent backend writes

evals.prompt: I am checking our self-hosted CopilotKit runtime and want to run npx copilotkit verify on production as the first check. What exact flags are safe, and does --round-trip call the AI or save anything?
evals.expected_output: Uses --expect-runtime oss and an agent ID for wiring-only validation first; avoids --round-trip by default; explains that --round-trip sends a live model request, consumes credits and creates a thread, and should only run in an authorized QA environment with known runtime URL and credentials.
expectations: Starts with a non-round-trip OSS wiring check using --expect-runtime oss and --agent
States --round-trip sends a real request that incurs model cost and creates a thread
Uses explicit authorized QA target and avoids default live production mutation

evals.prompt: We upgraded MDE from CopilotKit 1.75 to 1.84.1. The SAN-1630 A2UI catalog does not show in /chat even though TypeScript compiles. How should we proceed?
evals.expected_output: Checks current package pins, exact v1.84.1 exports, per-run render_ui tool/context propagation through LoggingMastraAgent, AG-UI tool-call stream and browser before creating a catalog; preserves useRenderTool fallback and avoids a parallel runtime.
expectations: Treats v1.75.0 references as historical and uses the current installed package
Demands an actual render_ui round trip through Mastra before claiming native A2UI works
Keeps existing tool renderer, runtime and route-specific providers

evals.prompt: Add interactive rental comparison and Events tickets with CopilotKit GenerativeUISurface. Can we copy the official generative-ui-shop, put model prices into cards and let the agent open Stripe Checkout itself?
evals.expected_output: Models only the bounded Surface/fallback pattern from pinned example, hydrates existing authorized current IDs through MDE services, reuses maps and cards, and requires user-activated checkout plus server-side price/quantity/availability validation and signed Stripe webhook.
expectations: Does not copy TanStack/Prisma/shop stack or add a second provider
Rejects model-provided prices, made-up coordinates and direct AI payment
Requires real E2E browser/Stripe TEST proof with deterministic fallback

evals.prompt: Use CopilotKit A2UI to build SAN-1630 for our existing Mastra app. The docs show a2ui: {} and an older A2A restaurant example. Should we add both of those plus the native render_ui catalog?
evals.expected_output: Routes to a2ui-protocol.md and native-generative-ui.md, distinguishes protocol middleware from native Components/Surfaces, rejects copying A2A v0.8 operations or adding a2ui: {} just to get render_ui, and requires installed-source/real-browser proof.
expectations: Separates protocol A2UI middleware from native render_ui without a second runtime
Recognizes legacy A2A/v0.8 payloads are not compatible with current spec by assumption
Requires exact package verification and one live tool-call/UI trace

evals.prompt: For MDE rentals, use the 69 CopilotKit standardUI components including Map and Button, and extend standardUI so the model can only render RentalCard. Is this the smallest safe catalog?
evals.expected_output: Routes to standard-catalog.md, explains extends: [standardUI] exposes all standard built-ins rather than narrowing them, recommends a tiny ID-only domain catalog and existing MDE map, and avoids installing MapLibre or AI-triggered checkout.
expectations: Explains 69-component standardUI and how extends expands visibility
Keeps MDE domain cards and existing map/pins authoritative
Never lets the agent invent prices/coordinates or trigger checkout

evals.prompt: An agent produced JSON with beginRendering/surfaceUpdate from the CopilotKit A2A starter, but our installed A2UI renderer expects createSurface/updateComponents/updateDataModel. Should we parse and run it anyway?
evals.expected_output: Routes to a2ui-protocol.md, identifies the starter's legacy v0.8 operation format versus v0.9+ and v1.0-candidate boundaries, rejects unvalidated mixing, and requires matching renderer/spec version, bounded catalog validation, negative tests and actual UI proof.
expectations: Rejects silently mixing A2UI operation versions
Uses a2ui.org and installed CopilotKit docs/types as sources of truth
Tests malformed/unsupported operations and auth-safe fallback
